speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) how does the Ministry address insurers which raise base Integrated Shield Plan premiums, effectively negating new rider savings; (b) what specific mechanisms ensure claims are not unreasonably rejected to mitigate rising costs; and (c) whether the Ministry will mandate greater transparency in premium calculation methods and publicly penalise insurers that engage in unjustifiable price hikes.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry was aware of the intention by insurers to raise base Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums at the same time as the required changes to IP rider specifications from 1 April 2026; and (b) if so, whether any and what analysis was done on how base premium increases would interact with rider changes in affecting overall premiums for consumers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers review the premiums of IPs and riders every year.
We have responded to previous similar Parliamentary Question Nos 1 to 4 asked by the Members at the 24 September 2025 Sitting, on increases in IP and rider premiums.
To recap, Government's role is to ensure affordable, accessible and quality subsidised healthcare for Singaporeans, with MediShield Life coming in to cover higher bills.
IPs and riders are private, commercial products that supplement MediShield Life coverage for unsubsidised healthcare.
To Mr Yip's question on claims management, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and MOH require insurance companies to uphold their contractual obligations and process claims in a fair manner.
Under MAS' insurance regulations, insurers must notify their policyholders of any change in policy terms and conditions at least 30 days before it takes effect.

Should there be disputes over specific claims, policyholders can take it to the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre (FIDReC), an independent and impartial institution that assists with insurance-related disputes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many Singaporeans are already facing rising premiums year after year.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As we have seen recently, even with cheaper riders, base premiums continue increasing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: So, households may still have to pay more overall.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: So, will MOH consider imposing clearer limits or review triggers on premium increases?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My second supplementary question is for older Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They face the steepest premium increases and have the least flexibility to change or switch plans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, there is a whole cluster of cost increases because of that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There is also over-consumption and over-servicing, and that is just a result of over-generous products that we see in the market today.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this causes increase in the cost of healthcare, which then results in increased claims, which results in increased premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because for this to be sustainable, the providers will have to reprice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because otherwise, if we artificially limit it, it will not be sustainable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They will not be able to, then, pay out in accordance to what they need to if they do not adjust and make sure that they can sustain in the long run.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In the end, this will actually harm the policyholders because they may see reduction in the benefits or even market exits, which is going to be worse.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, what we do at MOH, is that we do not just look at why these increases are happening.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But we are looking at the root causes and trying to address the root causes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have rider reforms, which the Member has seen; and also, in the works, the development of not-for-profit private hospitals.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, all these measures, in totality, will help to moderate the increases.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But it is a reality that this will happen.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We note, though, that there are concerns and we will continue to monitor this and respond accordingly to make sure that healthcare cost remains affordable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This ties into the second point the Member is making, with regard to seniors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We note they are especially vulnerable, but I just want to assert the point that there are also practical pathways that can be taken because there are options now.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Seniors can, at the appropriate juncture, review or right-size their coverage in accordance to their needs as well as to their affordability at that moment in time.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And so, that is an assurance that we give to all Singaporeans, and we will continue to monitor to ensure that there will be affordable healthcare services and it is accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I hope that gives that assurance that we continue to monitor this, but at the same time, we need to appreciate that there are practical realities with regard to premium increases, but we also ensure that nobody will be left out or not to be able to have access to healthcare because of cost pressures.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I generally accept that the Ministry does not want to intervene in the arrangements within private insurance companies and in the private healthcare, but I am coming from an angle of not overburdening the public healthcare.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Because we do not want a sudden surge of patients from private healthcare going to the public hospitals.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: So, in that regard, I would like to ask if the Ministry has studied the components of bill sizes that have contributed to the recent increase in medical costs in the private healthcare.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Because we have had measures to cool down, for example, the cost attributed to doctor's fee sizes with fee benchmarks as well as panel arrangements.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: So, has the Ministry studied whether other components – for example, facility costs, consumable costs and whether these have been riding steadily and whether there are plans to have similar benchmarks for these bill size components?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Following on to that, can I also ask the Ministry whether it has studied the effects of the panel arrangements on whether they have equitably kept doctors' fee sizes manageable compared to the fee benchmark that the Ministry already has?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Because my worry is that with entrenching panel behaviours by insurers, that we are also limiting access to equitable healthcare in the private sector.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the panel arrangement, I believe we had a discussion also in a previous Sitting about why this came about.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Really, it is going back to the whole big picture about insurers moderating the costs and how they can remain sustainable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because claims are high and because there is over-consumption, over-servicing, they then need to make sure that they are moderating their costs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And this becomes an administrative effort in their effort to try and moderate the payouts by actually empanelling members so that they can limit their cost to those who fit their structures.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This remains something that will be an enduring feature because this is a market reaction to something that is causing a pressure on the insurer's part.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, while we will take a position where we must protect the consumers and there must be fairness in all interactions with the panel doctors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As the Member know, we are quite robust in actually putting errant doctors to task, if, let us say, they have not done it properly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are sending out clinical guidelines to make sure that people are following proper care protocols and not just treating based on what they have as insurance policies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, these are all multi-pronged approaches and efforts that we are putting in place to ensure that we are responding to some of the concerns in this space.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is just a symptom, so the underlying cost pressures still need to be addressed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The description that we had put earlier in the past is that it is a knot that we need to untangle; and that is something we are doing with a multi-pronged, with engagements with different parties and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Hamid Razak, you have a short supplementary question to ask?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: I just want to mention for the record that I declare that I am an orthopaedic surgeon in private practice, and also a visiting consultant at public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My supplementary question to the Minister of State is, I accept that a primary driver of premium increases is rising healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But there is also other levers, such as reducing administrative costs at insurers themselves.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, the insurance industry as a whole has a big effort towards driving down administrative costs, third-party processor costs, claims processing costs, things like that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, how we intervene is via the conditions that are put in place vis-a-vis the consumers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We note how there should be adherence to deductibles as well as the co-payment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, these are things that we take a measured approach on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: What the Member suggests is a dimension of the cost components.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will not preclude us from having just general conversations with insurers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I just wanted to express the point that, while we do engage insurers quite robustly, we are very conscious about the fact that we also have to draw a line somewhere because it is a commercial product and we have to have them remain competitive.
